I ranked C1 first because its value is large compared with the other capacitors, and the symptoms fit an oversized feedback capacitor. This is a hand-estimate, not a full simulation.

The filter is a unity-gain Sallen-Key (R1, R2, C1, C2) preceded by an RC section (R0, C0). In that topology, increasing C1 lowers the cutoff and raises Q, so peaking rises. That matches the measured drop in fc to about 0.53× target and the increase in peaking to 6.8 dB. Since C2 would lower Q if increased, it is less likely. R2 is the second candidate because increasing it has the same qualitative effect. C0 is a weaker third candidate.
